The study used a high heat flux rig to evaluate the CMAS infiltration and degradation mechanisms.
The temperature range used in the high heat flux rig testing was between 2000°F to 3200°F (1093°C to 1750°C).
The study used a burner rig to evaluate the CMAS infiltration and degradation mechanisms in high-pressure and high-temperature conditions.
The temperature range used in the burner rig testing was between 1250°C to 1400°C.
The laser high heat flux rig was used to evaluate the CMAS infiltration and degradation mechanisms in high-temperature conditions with a high heat flux.
The study used cyclic testing to evaluate the durability and life of the coatings under repeated thermal cycles.
The ytterbium silicate EBC/HfO-Si bond coat on SiC/SiC CMC substrate was found to be a promising material for environmental barrier coatings.
The Air Force CMAS composition was found to be more resistant to degradation than conventional CMAS.
The study used a 2” diameter thermal barrier coated disc (back cooled) for the initial test in the high-pressure burner rig.
The thermal barrier coating temperature was 1250°C during the initial test.
The rig conditions included jet fuel & air combustion with mass air flow 1.5 lbm/s and 10 atmospheres (160 psi) pressure.
CMAS was injected after the burner nozzle but not fully melted and infiltrated during the initial test.
The study found that localized spallation and high erosion rates occurred in high CMAS concentration areas.
The researchers identified the CMAS composition, deposition, and aero aspects being initially investigated in high-pressure burner rig environments.
The study found that furnace cyclic testing of infiltrated coating specimens is planned.
